reasons: Classification is correct: the § 2(a) grant runs to Client alone with no affiliates, no contractors and no notice mechanic to add them, and § 15 permits consent-free assignment only to a financially responsible affiliate — so the clause misses both limbs of the fallback (affiliates on written notice; transfer to an M&A successor), making this a genuine deviation rather than an acceptable fallback being upgraded.

Redline is valid and directionally correct: it inserts 'its affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf' into the grant and adds successor-in-interest transfer to the assignment clause, tracking the redline guidance without disturbing surrounding commercial terms.

Edits are minimal in substance despite the advisory change ratios — the inserted language is confined to the two operative phrases the rule targets; no unnecessary rewriting of the grant scope, term or the § 2(a) non-exclusivity carve-out.

Rule is addressed completely for this contract: revocability was correctly assessed as absent (deterministic check confirms no at-will revocation), and the rationale properly notes this is not walk-away territory rather than over-escalating.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the [Playbook] prefix, explains the two changes and their commercial reason, and cites the playbook position without lecturing.
